name: Affenpinscher
description: A wiry-coated toy breed with a monkey-like face and a comedian's sense of timing, the Affenpinscher was bred to rat in German kitchens and never lost the attitude. He is fearless to the point of absurdity and treats obedience as a negotiation rather than a rule.
vibe_summary: A bearded little anarchist who thinks he's the biggest dog in the room.

name: Afghan Hound
description: An ancient sighthound built to course game across Afghan mountains, draped in silk and utterly indifferent to your opinion. The Afghan is sweet with his own people but famously aloof, and his coat demands hours of brushing every week.
vibe_summary: Supermodel aloofness with a sprinter's engine underneath the hair.

name: Airedale Terrier
description: The 'King of Terriers' is the largest of the family, a Yorkshire-bred all-rounder that has worked as hunter, wartime messenger, and police dog. He is clever, athletic, and mischievous, with a stubborn streak that needs an owner who finds terrier logic funny rather than infuriating.
vibe_summary: A big, bold problem-solver who will outthink a bored owner.

name: Akita
description: Japan's dignified guardian breed, famous for Hachiko-level loyalty and a near-total indifference to strangers and strange dogs. The Akita is quiet, clean, and profoundly devoted to his family, but he is a serious dog who requires experienced, consistent handling.
vibe_summary: Silent samurai loyalty — devoted to you, unmoved by everyone else.

name: Alaskan Malamute
description: The heavy-freight sled dog of the Arctic, built for pulling loads over long distances rather than for speed. Malamutes are affectionate, howly, and hilariously stubborn, and they will dig, roam, and blow enough coat to knit a second dog.
vibe_summary: A woolly, wolf-adjacent freight train who howls instead of barks.

name: All-Star Rescue Mutt
description: The great American everydog: a one-of-a-kind blend whose shuffled genetics tend to deliver moderate energy, sturdy health, and a temperament sanded smooth of purebred extremes. No two are alike, which is exactly the point — somewhere in a shelter right now is the specific mutt calibrated for your specific life.
vibe_summary: One of one, genetically lucky, and already looking for you.

name: American Bulldog
description: A powerful farm utility dog from the American South, kept athletic and functional where the English Bulldog went ornamental. He is confident, physical, and deeply bonded to his family, and he needs early socialization plus an owner who can handle real strength on a leash.
vibe_summary: A farmhand bruiser with a soft spot the size of Georgia.

name: American Eskimo Dog
description: A dazzling white Nordic spitz that earned its fame as a circus trick dog, and it shows — Eskies learn routines faster than most owners can invent them. They are vocal, watchful, and intensely people-oriented, sulking hard when left out of family life.
vibe_summary: A snow-white circus brain that narrates everything it sees.

name: American Foxhound
description: George Washington helped develop this rangy, sweet-natured pack hound, and it remains what it was in 1785: a tireless runner with a melodious bawl and a mild, easygoing disposition toward every person and dog it meets. It is one of America's rarest AKC breeds as a companion, largely because few homes can absorb its mileage requirements.
vibe_summary: A founding father's marathon dog, all stamina and song.

name: American Pit Bull Terrier
description: Athletic, eager, and famously human-affectionate, the APBT is a grinning velcro dog with an engine, not the caricature his reputation suggests. He needs real exercise, careful dog-dog management, and an owner ready to navigate housing and insurance restrictions on his behalf.
vibe_summary: A full-body wag with gladiator muscles and a marshmallow heart.

name: American Staffordshire Terrier
description: The show-ring cousin of the pit bull, stockier and slightly mellower but cut from the same devoted, muscular cloth. AmStaffs are confident and trainable people-pleasers who thrive on structure and shrivel when isolated in a backyard.
vibe_summary: A stocky, smiley bodyguard who lives for your approval.

name: Anatolian Shepherd
description: A Turkish livestock guardian bred for millennia to make life-or-death decisions alone on the steppe, and he has not forgotten it. Calm and rock-steady with his flock and family, he is territorial, independent, and entirely unsuited to owners who expect eager obedience.
vibe_summary: An ancient night-shift security contractor who answers to no one.

name: Australian Cattle Dog
description: Bred to drive cattle across brutal Australian outback distances, the heeler is one of the toughest, sharpest working dogs alive. He bonds ferociously to one person, invents jobs when unemployed, and will nip heels — including small children's — because it is literally what he was built to do.
vibe_summary: A tireless outback workaholic who considers rest a design flaw.

name: Australian Kelpie
description: The dog that runs across the backs of sheep in Australian mustering videos, the Kelpie is a heat-hardened working machine with stamina and problem-solving ability that rival any Border Collie. As a pet it needs a genuine daily job; without one, it will invent projects you won't approve of.
vibe_summary: An outback workaholic who considers rest a design flaw.

name: Australian Shepherd
description: The rodeo-circuit ranch dog of the American West, merle-coated, wickedly smart, and happiest with a job list. Aussies are stunning trail and sport partners, but an under-exercised one will herd your children, your guests, and your vacuum with equal commitment.
vibe_summary: A gorgeous overachiever who needs a job title, not a couch.

name: Basenji
description: The 'barkless dog' of Central Africa yodels instead of barking, grooms itself like a cat, and regards human commands as interesting suggestions. Basenjis are clean, curious escape artists who will climb fences and unspool your life the moment they get bored.
vibe_summary: A cat wearing a dog costume, with a yodel and an escape plan.

name: Basset Hound
description: Sixty pounds of scent hound on six-inch legs, the Basset trails rabbits with a nose second only to the Bloodhound's. He is mellow, stubborn, and sociable, happiest ambling behind a smell with a person or another dog for company, then sleeping it off loudly.
vibe_summary: A droopy, unhurried philosopher led entirely by his nose.

name: Beagle
description: A merry pack hound built to trail rabbits all day and sing about it, which is exactly what he will do in your backyard. Beagles are sturdy, funny, and wonderful with kids, but their nose overrides their ears — recall and diets are lifelong projects.
vibe_summary: A cheerful nose with a howl attached, forever following a scent.

name: Bearded Collie
description: A bouncing, shaggy Scottish droving dog whose signature move — the 'Beardie bounce' — was bred in to spot sheep over highland bracken. He is exuberant, clownish, and weatherproof, with a long coat that mats fast without serious weekly brushing.
vibe_summary: A shaggy highland tigger who bounces first and asks later.

name: Beauceron
description: France's imposing farm general herds, guards, and thinks with equal seriousness — a black-and-tan powerhouse whose motto is often given as "a strong mind in a strong body." It matures slowly, tests boundaries deliberately, and belongs with experienced owners who train with calm authority.
vibe_summary: A French field marshal who expects competence from his humans.

name: Bedlington Terrier
description: Shaped like a lamb and historically game enough to fight badgers, the Bedlington is the terrier world's great optical illusion. Modern lines are gentle, springy housemates with a curly, nearly shed-free coat, though the old racing and ratting fire flickers on whenever something small bolts.
vibe_summary: A lamb costume over a retired prizefighter.

name: Belgian Malinois
description: The dog that raids compounds with Navy SEALs: faster, lighter, and more intense than the German Shepherd it resembles. In the right working or sport home the Malinois is sublime; in a pet home without hours of daily training he becomes seventy pounds of teeth-forward anxiety.
vibe_summary: A special-forces missile that should never be someone's first dog.

name: Berger Picard
description: This tousled French sheepdog with expressive amber eyes nearly vanished after two world wars and remains rare even in France. Athletic and observant with a famously human-like gaze, it is devoted to its family, standoffish with strangers, and sulky if training turns harsh or repetitive.
vibe_summary: A scruffy French philosopher who herds with his eyebrows.

name: Bernedoodle
description: A Bernese Mountain Dog crossed with a Poodle, aiming for the Berner's tricolor sweetness with the Poodle's brains and low-shed coat — and a longer lifespan than the tragically short-lived Berner. Coats and temperaments vary by litter, and that plush fleece needs professional grooming every few weeks.
vibe_summary: A tricolor teddy bear engineered for cuddles and clean sofas.

name: Bernese Mountain Dog
description: A tricolor Swiss farm dog bred to pull carts and adore children, wrapped in one of dogdom's most beautiful coats. The heartbreak is the lifespan: cancer rates cut the average Berner's life brutally short, so every year with one is deliberately treasured.
vibe_summary: A gentle alpine giant who loves hugely and leaves too soon.

name: Bichon Frise
description: A powder-puff charmer descended from Mediterranean sailors' dogs and French court favorites, built entirely around delighting people. The Bichon is cheerful, low-shedding, and great in apartments, but that white cloud of coat requires monthly professional grooming to stay a cloud.
vibe_summary: A giggling cotton ball whose entire career is being adored.

name: Black Russian Terrier
description: Engineered by the Soviet Red Star kennel to patrol borders in Russian winters, the "Blackie" is a massive, coated guardian that glues itself to its family and takes perimeter security personally. It is calmer and more biddable than most giant guards, but its size and suspicion demand a confident, experienced handler.
vibe_summary: A Soviet-engineered bear who reports directly to your family.

name: Bloodhound
description: The most powerful nose in the animal kingdom's service, whose trailing evidence is admissible in some courtrooms. Off the trail he is a wrinkled, drooly, affectionate lump — but on a scent he is deaf to your existence, so fences and leashes are non-negotiable.
vibe_summary: A forensic instrument wrapped in wrinkles and slobber.

name: Bluetick Coonhound
description: Named for its striking blue-mottled coat, the Bluetick is a cold-trailing specialist with a booming, musical bawl and the patience to work a scent for hours. Off the trail it is affectionate and houndishly laid-back, though neighbors within earshot will learn its voice by heart.
vibe_summary: A blue-speckled baritone with a bloodhound's patience.

name: Boerboel
description: South Africa's farm mastiff was bred to face leopards and defend remote homesteads, and it remains one of the most physically powerful and territorially serious dogs money can buy. With its family — children included — it is calm and affectionate; ownership is nonetheless an expert-level commitment, full stop.
vibe_summary: A homestead fortress that happens to adore its own children.

name: Bolognese
description: A fluffy white companion from Renaissance Italy, the Bolognese is the Bichon's calmer, more serious cousin — content to shadow one beloved person from room to room all day. It is easygoing and low-shedding but genuinely miserable when left alone, so it suits homes where someone is usually around.
vibe_summary: A Renaissance lapdog who has chosen you as a life project.

name: Border Collie
description: Widely considered the most intelligent dog on earth, bred on the Anglo-Scottish border to move sheep with eye contact alone. That genius is a contract: give a Border Collie daily work for body and brain or he will find his own projects, none of which you will approve of.
vibe_summary: A PhD in an athlete's body who will not tolerate unemployment.

name: Border Terrier
description: An otter-headed working terrier from the English-Scottish border, tough enough to run with foxhounds yet uncommonly good-natured at home. He is the rare terrier that genuinely likes other dogs and children, though squirrels remain a declared enemy for life.
vibe_summary: The terrier for people who thought they didn't like terriers.

name: Borzoi
description: The Russian wolfhound of tsarist hunting parties: a silken, long-nosed sighthound capable of 35 mph and profound indoor laziness. Borzoi are quiet, gentle, and cat-like with their affection, but any small fleeing animal flips an ancient, unstoppable chase switch.
vibe_summary: Aristocratic couch sculpture, occasionally deployed at 35 mph.

name: Boston Terrier
description: The 'American Gentleman' wears a tuxedo coat and the manners to match — a compact, dapper city dog invented in Boston in the 1870s. He is playful, portable, and easy to live with, though his flat face means snoring, gassiness, and real caution in summer heat.
vibe_summary: A tuxedoed city gentleman with a snort and a sense of humor.

name: Bouvier des Flandres
description: A burly, beard-faced Belgian farm dog that once drove cattle, pulled carts, and hauled wounded soldiers off Flanders battlefields. Calm and steady with his family and naturally suspicious of outsiders, he combines guardian gravity with a coat that traps mud, snow, and half his dinner.
vibe_summary: A grave, bearded farm foreman who takes his household seriously.

name: Boxer
description: A German working breed that stayed a puppy at heart: Boxers famously don't mature until three, if ever, and greet life with full-body wiggles and paw-swats. They are patient with kids and instinctively protective, but the shortened muzzle and high cancer rates shadow the breed's health.
vibe_summary: A perpetual toddler in a bodybuilder's frame, wiggling at full power.

name: Boykin Spaniel
description: South Carolina's official state dog was bred small enough to share a swamp boat and tough enough to retrieve ducks in southern heat all day. The "little brown dog" brings that same merry, eager-to-please engine home, making it one of the most livable of the true hunting spaniels.
vibe_summary: A swamp-boat retriever with a tail that never stops.

name: Bracco Italiano
description: Italy's ancient pointer moves through the field at a distinctive extended trot and through the living room like a doleful, affectionate houseguest who takes up more couch than expected. Gentle and sensitive despite its houndy grandeur, it works best with soft-handed training and generous jowl-towel budgets.
vibe_summary: A soulful Italian gentleman with magnificent, drippy jowls.

name: Briard
description: France's shaggy 'heart wrapped in fur,' a flock guardian-herder hybrid that served as a WWI sentry and medic dog. Briards are fiercely loyal and surprisingly sensitive under all that hair, but their independence and protectiveness demand a confident, committed owner and hours of coat care.
vibe_summary: A shaggy French romantic who guards his people like a vow.

name: Brittany
description: A compact French bird dog that points and retrieves with boundless orange-and-white enthusiasm, often called the most athletic dog per pound. Brittanys are sweet, eager, and soft-tempered, but their energy is genuinely sporting-grade — a walk around the block is a warm-up, not a workout.
vibe_summary: A featherweight bird-dog dynamo running on pure eagerness.

name: Brussels Griffon
description: A bearded Belgian stable ratter turned lapdog, with an almost-human expression that inspired the Ewoks. Griffs bond obsessively to one person, take offense easily, and carry themselves with a self-importance completely uncorrelated with their nine pounds.
vibe_summary: A tiny, bearded emotional-support gargoyle with one chosen human.

name: Bull Terrier
description: The egg-headed gladiator turned family jester, instantly recognizable and constitutionally incapable of taking anything seriously. Bull Terriers are muscular, mischievous three-year-olds for life, prone to obsessive spinning and tail-chasing if under-stimulated.
vibe_summary: An egg-headed comedian built like a keg and wired for mischief.

name: Bullmastiff
description: Bred by English gamekeepers to knock poachers down and hold them without mauling, the Bullmastiff still guards by mass and presence rather than noise. At home he is a mellow, low-exercise shadow who believes he fits on your lap, but his size and stubbornness demand early training.
vibe_summary: A silent, 115-pound doorman who mostly naps on the job.

name: Cairn Terrier
description: The scrappy Highland rat-hunter that played Toto, still every inch the shaggy, fearless little digger the Scots bred to bolt vermin from rock piles. Cairns are hardy, cheerful, and busy, happiest with a family that laughs at their bossiness and hides the flowerbeds.
vibe_summary: Toto with a shovel: small, scrappy, and always mid-project.

name: Canaan Dog
description: Redomesticated from free-living pariah dogs of the Israeli desert, the Canaan Dog carries survivor instincts intact: sharp territorial alarm, deep wariness of the unfamiliar, and rugged, low-maintenance health. It is devoted and clever with its own family but never stops thinking like a dog that once had to look after itself.
vibe_summary: A desert survivor who trusts its family and audits everyone else.

name: Cane Corso
description: Italy's descendant of Roman war dogs, a sleek, imposing mastiff that guards family and farm with quiet, calculating intensity. The Corso is deeply loyal and surprisingly trainable, but he is a serious guardian who will make his own security decisions unless an experienced owner makes them first.
vibe_summary: A Roman bodyguard in a black velvet suit — loyal, watchful, not a starter dog.

name: Cardigan Welsh Corgi
description: The older, tailed, big-eared Corgi — a Welsh cattle driver a thousand years deep, slightly more reserved and houndier than his Pembroke cousin. Cardigans are adaptable, funny, and devoted, with a full herding brain riding surprisingly low to the ground.
vibe_summary: The Corgi with the tail: a full-size farm brain on legroom-economy legs.

name: Catahoula Leopard Dog
description: Louisiana's swamp-bred hog and cattle dog, splashed in merle and often glass-eyed, tough enough to work feral livestock through bayou country. Catahoulas are independent, territorial, and relentless workers who need land, a job, and an owner who out-stubborns them.
vibe_summary: A leopard-spotted bayou workhorse with zero interest in suburbia.

name: Cavalier King Charles Spaniel
description: A silky lap spaniel bred by British royalty for exactly one job — companionship — and arguably the best in the world at it. Cavaliers adore everyone they meet and adapt to nearly any household, but heart disease (mitral valve) is endemic in the breed and shapes its shorter lifespan.
vibe_summary: Pure liquid affection in royal packaging; loves you and everyone else too.

name: Cavapoo
description: A Cavalier crossed with a Miniature Poodle, designed to blend the spaniel's melting sweetness with the Poodle's wits and low-shed curls. The result is one of the friendliest small companions available, though the coat needs regular grooming and the dog needs near-constant company.
vibe_summary: A curly-coated cuddle algorithm optimized for lap time.

name: Chesapeake Bay Retriever
description: The toughest retriever, bred to break ice in the Chesapeake and haul hundreds of ducks a day, with an oily coat that shrugs off freezing water. Unlike the everybody's-friend Lab, the Chessie is one-family loyal, discerning with strangers, and stubborn enough to need a genuinely consistent trainer.
vibe_summary: The Lab's flinty waterman cousin — tougher, cooler, choosier.

name: Chihuahua
description: The world's smallest dog carries its ancient Mexican lineage with the confidence of a breed fifty times its size, bonding intensely with one person and auditing everyone else. Chihuahuas are long-lived, portable, and fierce, but they are not toys for small children and they know it.
vibe_summary: Five pounds of unshakable opinion and single-person devotion.

name: Chihuahua Mix
description: Chi mixes dominate shelter small-dog rooms, especially across the Sun Belt, and blending in other breeds usually softens the Chihuahua's edge while keeping the fierce one-person devotion and marathon lifespan. Cheap to feed, easy to house, and built to love you well into their teens, they are the most underrated adoption bargain going.
vibe_summary: A pocket-sized loyalist with fifteen good years to give you.

name: Chinese Crested
description: A mostly-hairless lapdog with punk-rock tufts at the head, feet, and tail, kept aboard trading ships as a ratter and heater. Cresteds are cheerful, agile velcro dogs whose exposed skin needs sunscreen and sweaters — grooming traded for skincare.
vibe_summary: A naked little hot-water bottle with a rockstar hairdo.

name: Chow Chow
description: An ancient Chinese guardian with a lion's ruff, a blue-black tongue, and the emotional availability of a housecat. Chows are clean, quiet, and fiercely loyal to their few chosen people, but they neither need nor want strangers' affection and they never pretend otherwise.
vibe_summary: A dignified lion-cat who tolerates exactly three people on earth.

name: Clumber Spaniel
description: The heavyweight of the spaniel family trundles through cover with unhurried thoroughness and brings the same dignified, low-key amiability home. A favorite of British aristocracy, the Clumber is sweet, sleepy, and shed-and-drool generous — a mellow companion for owners with lint rollers at the ready.
vibe_summary: A dozing duke of a spaniel, all patience and white fur on your trousers.

name: Cockapoo
description: The original doodle, crossing Cocker Spaniel warmth with Poodle intelligence since the 1960s — decades before the designer-dog boom. Cockapoos are adaptable, people-centered family dogs with low-shed coats, though quality varies widely with the breeder and the curls still need regular clipping.
vibe_summary: The friendly original doodle: happy anywhere, as long as you're there.

name: Cocker Spaniel
description: The smallest sporting breed and a mid-century American icon, all pleading eyes and silky ears, bred originally to flush woodcock. A well-bred Cocker is merry and gentle, but the breed's popularity boom left lines with anxious temperaments, and those glamorous ears invite chronic infections.
vibe_summary: The soft-eyed golden-age sweetheart who just wants to be near you.

name: Collie (Rough)
description: Lassie's breed, and the legend is roughly accurate: the Rough Collie is gentle, intuitive, and almost eerily attuned to children and household moods. She is milder than most herders — devoted without being frantic — though the magnificent coat sheds in drifts and the breed likes to narrate with barking.
vibe_summary: Lassie was a documentary: a gentle guardian angel in a fur coat.

name: Coton de Tulear
description: Madagascar's 'Royal Dog,' named for its cotton-soft white coat and legendary for clowning, vocal chattering, and walking on its hind legs to amuse people. Cotons are hardy, long-lived little companions who take their comedy seriously and their separation badly.
vibe_summary: A cotton-soft island comedian who performs for an audience of you.

name: Dachshund
description: Germany's badger dog: a long, low excavation unit with a full-size hound bark and the courage to follow a badger underground. Dachshunds are funny, devoted, and famously stubborn, and their long backs mean stairs, jumping, and extra weight are lifelong hazards.
vibe_summary: A big dog compiled into a small, stubborn, sausage-shaped binary.

name: Dalmatian
description: Bred to trot for miles beside horse-drawn carriages, the Dalmatian is a marathon athlete first and a movie star second. He is loyal and striking but intense, mouthy in adolescence, and prone to deafness and urinary stones — a working dog too often bought as decor.
vibe_summary: A spotted endurance athlete who is far more dog than the movie promised.

name: Doberman Pinscher
description: Engineered in the 1890s by a German tax collector who wanted protection on his rounds, the Doberman is sleek, brilliant, and bottomlessly loyal. Modern lines are softer and more velcro than the guard-dog stereotype, but the brains and drive are intact, and dilated cardiomyopathy stalks the breed.
vibe_summary: A velvet-coated bodyguard who sleeps under your blankets.

name: Dogo Argentino
description: Argentina's white big-game hunter, bred to run down wild boar in a pack and still guard the family truck afterward. The Dogo is athletic, affectionate with his people, and immensely powerful, with prey drive and dog-aggression genetics that make him strictly an experienced-owner breed — and banned in several countries.
vibe_summary: A white marble boar-hunter: majestic, devoted, absolutely not casual.

name: Dutch Shepherd
description: The brindle all-rounder of Dutch farms, rescued from near-extinction by police and sport-dog trainers who prize its balance of drive and level-headedness. Slightly steadier than the Malinois but cut from the same working cloth, the Dutchie thrives on training and wilts without a job.
vibe_summary: The Malinois's brindle cousin with a slightly better off switch.

name: English Bulldog
description: The wrinkled national mascot of England, re-engineered from bull-baiter into one of dogdom's most amiable couch ornaments. His charm is immense and his needs are few, but the flat face and extreme build bring breathing, skin, and joint problems that make him one of the most vet-intensive breeds you can own.
vibe_summary: A snoring gargoyle of pure affection with a fragile chassis.

name: English Cocker Spaniel
description: The "merry cocker" earns its nickname with a perpetually wagging rear end and an enthusiasm for life that survives rain, mud, and Mondays. Leggier and more field-capable than its American cousin, it balances real bird-dog drive with one of the sweetest household temperaments in the sporting group.
vibe_summary: Perpetual-motion cheerfulness with the softest ears in the room.

name: English Mastiff
description: The heaviest breed on earth guards its family with sheer presence rather than aggression, spending most of the day as a snoring, drooling landmark in your living room. Its needs are modest but everything it does touch, from food bills to vet costs to the slobber radius, is enormous.
vibe_summary: Two hundred pounds of quiet devotion and airborne drool.

name: English Setter
description: The 'gentleman of the dog world,' a speckled (belton) bird dog that freezes into a stylish set when it finds game. English Setters are mellow and affectionate in the house yet genuinely athletic outside — the classic hunt-hard, nap-hard sporting dog, sweet-tempered to a fault.
vibe_summary: A speckled aristocrat: all business in the field, all cuddle at home.

name: English Springer Spaniel
description: Named for the way it 'springs' game from cover, this is the classic rough-shooting spaniel: tireless in the field, soppy on the sofa, and never more than six feet from its person. Springers are biddable and joyful, but field-line dogs carry serious energy and the breed hates being left alone.
vibe_summary: A mud-loving field dynamo who is also a professional lap warmer.

name: Entlebucher Mountain Dog
description: The smallest and quickest of the four Swiss mountain breeds, the Entlebucher is a muscular tricolor cattle-driver with a big laugh of a personality and a bodyguard's dedication to its people. It needs real exercise and a job, and it herds children, guests, and slow-moving adults on its own initiative.
vibe_summary: A compact Swiss taskmaster who keeps the whole household moving.

name: Field Spaniel
description: A rare, glossy-coated spaniel that sits temperamentally between the merry Cocker and the driving Springer: docile at home, workmanlike in the field, and quietly devoted throughout. Its sensitivity is real — it withers under harsh handling and blooms with gentle, consistent training.
vibe_summary: The spaniel family's thoughtful, underappreciated middle child.

name: Finnish Lapphund
description: Bred by the Sámi to herd reindeer above the Arctic Circle, the Lappie pairs a weatherproof teddy-bear coat with a famously kind, people-loving temperament and a herder's quick mind. It announces visitors with enthusiasm and sheds its dense undercoat in impressive seasonal storms.
vibe_summary: A reindeer-herding teddy bear with a heart full of people.

name: Flat-Coated Retriever
description: Nicknamed the Peter Pan of retrievers, the Flat-Coat stays exuberantly puppyish well into old age and greets everyone like a long-lost friend. The heartbreak is a well-documented cancer predisposition that keeps its lifespan shorter than its retriever cousins.
vibe_summary: A Golden Retriever's joy dialed to eleven, forever young at heart.

name: French Bulldog
description: America's most popular dog earned the crown by being a hilarious, low-exercise companion that thrives in a studio apartment. The flat face behind that charm brings serious breathing, spine, and heat problems, so budget for vet bills and skip summer midday walks.
vibe_summary: A bat-eared comedian built for city living, not marathons.

name: German Shepherd
description: The world's default police, military, and service dog for a reason: brilliant, biddable, and fiercely devoted to its own people. That devotion demands a real job and confident handling, and generations of popularity have left the breed with widespread hip and elbow problems.
vibe_summary: A loyal professional who needs a mission, not just a yard.

name: German Shorthaired Pointer
description: A do-everything hunting machine that points, retrieves, swims, and then asks what's next, all wrapped in a wash-and-wear ticked coat. Under-exercised GSPs invent their own jobs, usually involving your furniture, so this breed belongs with genuinely active owners.
vibe_summary: A tireless athlete who thinks your 10K is a warm-up.

name: German Wirehaired Pointer
description: The GSP's bristly, weatherproof cousin trades a little of that sunny sociability for more grit, more independence, and a coat that shrugs off briars and cold water. It bonds hard to its hunter but can be aloof and territorial with outsiders, and it needs field-dog levels of work.
vibe_summary: A bearded, all-weather hunter with opinions of its own.

name: Giant Schnauzer
description: A powerful, low-shedding guardian bred to drive cattle and guard Bavarian breweries, with the intelligence to run your household if you let it. This is a serious working dog that needs daily training, real exercise, and an owner it respects, not a first-timer's fluffy Schnauzer.
vibe_summary: A bearded bodyguard with a PhD and no patience for slackers.

name: Golden Retriever
description: The archetypal family dog: patient with kids, eager to please, and convinced every human on earth is a potential best friend. The trade-offs are constant shedding, a real need for daily activity, and a breed-wide cancer rate that responsible buyers should ask breeders about directly.
vibe_summary: Sunshine in dog form, happiest with a tennis ball and its whole family in view.

name: Goldendoodle
description: The Golden-Poodle cross took over suburbia by pairing a retriever's sociability with a coat that barely sheds, though that coat demands professional grooming every six to eight weeks. Quality varies wildly between breeders, so temperament and health depend heavily on where the puppy comes from.
vibe_summary: A teddy bear that loves everyone and bills you at the groomer.

name: Gordon Setter
description: The heaviest and most serious of the setters, a black-and-tan Scottish bird dog that is devoted to its family and politely reserved with everyone else. It matures slowly and needs long daily runs, rewarding patient owners with a steadier, more loyal temperament than its flashier Irish cousin.
vibe_summary: The setter that saves its heart for family, not the crowd.

name: Great Dane
description: The Apollo of dogs is a surprisingly mellow housemate that mostly wants a big couch and its people nearby, making it better in apartments than its size suggests. The costs are real: everything from food to medication scales with the dog, bloat is a constant risk, and eight years together goes fast.
vibe_summary: A horse-sized lapdog with a short, precious clock.

name: Great Pyrenees
description: A livestock guardian bred to make life-or-death decisions alone on a mountainside, which is exactly why it ignores your recall and barks at the night. Gentle and patient with its flock, human or otherwise, but it needs a fenced yard, tolerant neighbors, and an owner who respects its independence.
vibe_summary: A calm white mountain that guards everything and obeys no one.

name: Greater Swiss Mountain Dog
description: A striking tricolor draft dog that hauled carts through Alpine villages and now happily hauls kids around the backyard. Swissies are sturdier and shorter-coated than their Bernese cousins but share the giant-breed bargains: big appetites, joint concerns, and not enough years.
vibe_summary: A cheerful Alpine workhorse who thinks your family is the herd.

name: Greyhound
description: The fastest dog alive is, off the track, a professional napper that needs a couple of short sprints and then twenty hours of couch time. Retired racers make gentle, quiet, low-odor apartment dogs, though their prey drive means small fluffy animals and off-leash parks are usually off the table.
vibe_summary: A 45-mph couch potato who sprints for five minutes and sleeps for twenty hours.

name: Harrier
description: Sized neatly between the Beagle and the English Foxhound, the Harrier is a cheerful pack hunter built for hours of steady hare-trailing, and it brings that same sturdy sociability home. One of the AKC's rarest breeds, it is a happy, tolerant family dog for anyone who can outlast its stamina and its voice.
vibe_summary: A Beagle scaled up to marathon spec, rarity included.

name: Havanese
description: Cuba's national dog is a silky, springy extrovert that trains eagerly, travels well, and genuinely likes children, cats, and strangers alike. It was bred purely for companionship, so it handles being left alone poorly and its coat needs steady brushing or a standing groomer appointment.
vibe_summary: A velcro charmer from Havana who performs for any audience.

name: Hound Mix
description: Long ears, soulful eyes, and a nose that runs the show: hound mixes pour out of Southern shelters, blending Beagle, coonhound, and foxhound lines into easygoing, dog-loving companions built for both trail days and epic naps. They arrive pre-loaded with patience and a signature singing voice your neighbors will come to know.
vibe_summary: A soulful-eyed napper whose nose occasionally hijacks the walk.

name: Ibizan Hound
description: An elegant, deer-like sighthound from the Balearic Islands that can clear a six-foot fence from a standstill, so containment is non-negotiable. Quiet and polite indoors, it saves its intensity for anything small and fast that moves, which rules out most cat households.
vibe_summary: A graceful escape artist with ancient Egyptian looks and a rabbit obsession.

name: Icelandic Sheepdog
description: Iceland's only native breed arrived with the Vikings and spent a millennium herding sheep across lava fields, developing a curled tail, a weatherproof coat, and an irrepressibly cheerful bark-first personality. It is confident, playful, and so people-oriented that Icelanders traditionally let it sleep indoors — rare status for a working farm dog.
vibe_summary: A grinning Viking farmhand who narrates everything joyfully.

name: Irish Setter
description: A rollicking, mahogany-red bird dog whose glamour-coat hides a goofy, slow-maturing teenager that stays one until about age three. It needs serious daily running and inclusion in everything the family does; a bored Irish Setter left in the yard becomes a loud, destructive one.
vibe_summary: A red-carpet coat wrapped around a permanent adolescent.

name: Irish Terrier
description: The daredevil of the terrier world, a wiry red dog famous for courage far beyond its size and a deep, sometimes combative dislike of other dogs. With its own people it is playful, hardy, and low-shedding, one of the healthiest purebreds you can find.
vibe_summary: A fearless redhead who never starts trouble but never backs down.

name: Irish Water Spaniel
description: The tallest spaniel wears a liver-brown coat of tight, barely-shedding curls, a distinctive topknot, and a bare "rat tail" — and behind the odd looks lives the "clown of the spaniels," a smart, watery athlete with a genuine sense of humor. It is devoted to its family, standoffish with strangers, and happiest soaking wet.
vibe_summary: A curly-coated water comedian with a rat's tail and a big heart.

name: Irish Wolfhound
description: The tallest of all dog breeds is a shaggy, dignified gentle soul that once hunted wolves and now mostly wants to lean on you. Everything about it is oversized except the lifespan; heart disease and bone cancer make six to eight years the honest expectation.
vibe_summary: A mythic, gentle skyscraper on borrowed time.

name: Italian Greyhound
description: A miniature sighthound that alternates between rocket-launch zoomies and burrowing under your blanket for the rest of the day. Its needle-thin legs fracture easily and it despises cold, rain, and being alone, so this is a dog for gentle households and stocked sweater drawers.
vibe_summary: A shivering little aristocrat surgically attached to your lap.

name: Jack Russell Terrier
description: Fifteen pounds of fox-hunting intensity that can outlast most owners, out-dig most fences, and outsmart casual training. Channeled into sports or farm work it is brilliant and hilarious; treated as a lapdog it becomes a barking, spinning agent of chaos.
vibe_summary: A pocket-sized adrenaline junkie with a genius IQ and zero chill.

name: Japanese Chin
description: A refined little companion bred for Japanese nobility that behaves more like a cat: it perches on furniture backs, grooms itself fastidiously, and dispenses affection on its own schedule. Quiet and undemanding, it suits calm apartments but its flat face makes heat a genuine hazard.
vibe_summary: A cat wearing a dog costume, raised in a palace.

name: Keeshond
description: The smiling Dutch barge dog wears spectacle markings and treats its family like a full-time job, shadowing everyone from room to room. It is friendly to a fault with people but announces every visitor, squirrel, and delivery truck, and that magnificent double coat blows out twice a year.
vibe_summary: A grinning fluffball who loves everyone and narrates everything.

name: Kerry Blue Terrier
description: Ireland's blue-coated all-rounder once herded, hunted, and guarded farms, and it retains a working terrier's spark plus a notorious grudge against other dogs. The soft, non-shedding coat is a gift for allergy sufferers but requires committed trimming to avoid becoming a felted mess.
vibe_summary: A blue-collar Irish scrapper in a show coat.

name: Komondor
description: The corded Hungarian flock guardian looks like a mop and thinks like a night watchman, making independent decisions about who and what belongs on its property. The famous cords never brush out; they must be separated by hand and take a full day to dry, and the dog under them is emphatically not for beginners.
vibe_summary: A sentient security system disguised as a mop.

name: Kuvasz
description: Hungary's white guardian is intensely loyal to its own household and constitutionally suspicious of everyone else, a combination that demands early, lifelong socialization. It thrives with land to patrol and a job to do; suburban life without either turns its vigilance into a liability.
vibe_summary: A one-family bodyguard who never got the memo about guests.

name: Labradoodle
description: The original designer cross, bred in Australia for allergy-friendly guide work, blends Labrador enthusiasm with Poodle brains and a low-shed coat. Coat type and temperament vary more than the marketing admits, so meet the parents and expect real grooming bills either way.
vibe_summary: A bouncy, brainy crowd-pleaser in a shed-resistant suit.

name: Labrador Mix
description: America's favorite dog, remixed: Lab crosses fill shelters coast to coast, typically keeping the breed's famous friendliness and food-motivated trainability while hybrid vigor often smooths out purebred health issues. For most families wanting "basically a Lab," a Lab mix delivers the whole experience for an adoption fee.
vibe_summary: All the Lab love, extra genetic shuffle, waiting at your local shelter.

name: Labrador Retriever
description: Three decades as America's favorite dog rest on a simple formula: friendly with everyone, forgiving of training mistakes, and game for anything involving water, food, or a ball. The fine print is heavy year-round shedding, a bottomless appetite that invites obesity, and a rowdy adolescence that lasts past age two.
vibe_summary: The all-American good sport who never met a ball, a lake, or a snack it didn't love.

name: Lagotto Romagnolo
description: Italy's curly-coated truffle hunter is the rare working dog scaled for modern life: moderate size, huge nose, keen trainability, and a coat that barely sheds. Give that nose a job, whether scent games or actual truffles, or it will excavate your garden with professional thoroughness.
vibe_summary: A truffle-hunting teddy bear with a world-class nose.

name: Lakeland Terrier
description: Bred to bolt foxes from rocky dens in England's Lake District, this compact terrier packs big-dog confidence and remarkable durability into seventeen wiry pounds. It is cheekier and more independent than obedient, but its low-shedding coat and sturdy health make it an underrated companion.
vibe_summary: A cocky little fell-runner who fears nothing and sheds nothing.

name: Leonberger
description: A lion-maned German giant bred to look majestic and act gentle, famous for its patience with children and its love of swimming and cart-pulling. Owners sign up for astonishing quantities of hair and drool, giant-breed food bills, and a lifespan that rarely reaches double digits.
vibe_summary: A benevolent lion who thinks it's the family babysitter.

name: Lhasa Apso
description: A thousand years as sentinel of Tibetan monasteries produced a small dog with a big dog's self-possession: watchful, stubborn, and unimpressed by strangers. It is hardy and long-lived, content with modest exercise, and far more independent than its lapdog looks suggest.
vibe_summary: A tiny monastery guard who answers to no one, least of all you.

name: Maltese
description: Two thousand years of pure companionship breeding produced a fearless six-pound optimist in a floor-length white coat that never stops needing attention, and neither does the dog. It is gentler than most toys with its own people but too fragile for rough-handed toddlers.
vibe_summary: Six pounds of silk that believes it runs the household, correctly.

name: Maltipoo
description: The Maltese-Poodle cross delivers a soft, barely-shedding lapdog that trains more willingly than most toys and adapts to any living space that includes a human lap. It was engineered for togetherness, which means separation anxiety is the breed's real weak spot.
vibe_summary: A pocket-sized cloud whose only demand is that you never leave.

name: Miniature Pinscher
description: The self-styled King of Toys is not a shrunken Doberman but an older German ratter with a signature high-stepping gait and a fearless, self-important attitude. It is a hardy, low-grooming escape artist that will test every gap in your fence and every inch of your patience.
vibe_summary: A ten-pound dictator with a hackney-horse strut.

name: Miniature Poodle
description: The middle Poodle packs the breed's full intelligence and athleticism into a fifteen-pound frame that fits any home, and it lives long enough to learn your entire repertoire twice. The non-shedding coat is genuinely allergy-friendly but grows forever, so grooming is a fixed monthly expense.
vibe_summary: A compact genius who mastered your routine by Tuesday.

name: Miniature Schnauzer
description: The most popular Schnauzer earns its keep as a spirited, low-shedding family dog that is friendlier and more trainable than most terriers while keeping their alert, vocal edge. Its beard and wiry coat need regular grooming, and it will absolutely tell you about every squirrel.
vibe_summary: A mustachioed town crier who takes neighborhood watch very seriously.

name: Newfoundland
description: The legendary nanny dog and water-rescue specialist combines a lifeguard's instincts with a temperament so sweet it borders on saintly. In exchange you accept heroic shedding, ever-present drool, a dog that overheats in mild weather, and giant-breed heart and joint problems.
vibe_summary: A drooling, swimming saint who considers your kids his job.

name: Norfolk Terrier
description: The drop-eared half of the Norfolk-Norwich pair is one of the smallest working terriers and among the most companionable, happier in a lap than most of its cousins. It keeps enough ratting instinct to chase anything small, but its sturdy health and portable size make it a superb small-home dog.
vibe_summary: A pocket terrier that swapped some fire for extra cuddle.

name: Norwegian Elkhound
description: A Viking-era spitz built to track moose through snow and hold them at bay by barking, a skill it practices enthusiastically in suburbia. Hardy, independent, and nearly weatherproof, it is a devoted family dog for people who can live with the volume and the twice-yearly fur blizzard.
vibe_summary: A Viking shipmate with a foghorn bark and an arctic coat.

name: Norwich Terrier
description: The prick-eared sibling of the Norfolk carries a bit more spark and sass in the same twelve-pound package, originally bred to bolt rats and foxes alongside hunts. It is affectionate, portable, and unusually sociable for a terrier, though its rarity means long waitlists and real prices.
vibe_summary: A perky-eared imp with terrier fire in a handbag-sized frame.

name: Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever
description: The smallest retriever lures ducks within gunshot by playing at the water's edge, and that job description, playful, clever, and relentless, is exactly what you get at home. Tollers are more intense and more reserved with strangers than Goldens, and their piercing excitement scream is famous for a reason.
vibe_summary: A fox-red trickster with a retriever's heart and a banshee's scream.

name: Old English Sheepdog
description: The shaggy drover of English postcards is a clownish, adaptable family dog with a distinctive pot-casse bark and a herding habit of bumping wayward children back into line. That iconic coat is the catch: hours of weekly brushing or a standing appointment to keep it clipped short.
vibe_summary: A bumbling shag-carpet comedian who herds the kids for fun.

name: Otterhound
description: With fewer individuals worldwide than the giant panda, the shaggy, webbed-footed Otterhound is Britain's rarest native breed — a boisterous, deep-voiced swimmer originally packed against river otters. It is amiable, stubborn, and gloriously messy, flinging water and beard-drips with total unconcern.
vibe_summary: A rarer-than-panda river shag with a foghorn voice.

name: Papillon
description: Behind the butterfly ears is the sharpest mind in the toy group: Papillons routinely embarrass bigger dogs in agility and obedience rings. It is a robust, long-lived athlete in miniature that needs mental work, not just a lap, to stay civilized.
vibe_summary: A butterfly-eared genius who thinks agility trials are beneath its talent.

name: Pekingese
description: Bred for Chinese emperors and never allowed to forget it, the Pekingese moves through life with unhurried dignity and expects service, not commands. Its flat face and heavy mane make heat dangerous, and its independence makes housetraining a negotiation rather than a lesson.
vibe_summary: A tiny emperor who tolerates your presence, occasionally warmly.

name: Pembroke Welsh Corgi
description: A full-sized herding dog on ten-inch legs, the internet's favorite breed is smart, bossy, and convinced it should be managing the household. The cute exterior hides real herding-dog needs, a serious shedding habit, and a long back that punishes extra weight and staircases.
vibe_summary: A big dog compiled into a small, opinionated loaf.

name: Pharaoh Hound
description: Malta's national dog is a sleek rabbit courser that famously blushes, its ears and nose flushing rose-pink when excited. It is calmer and more affectionate indoors than most sighthounds but shares their non-negotiables: a fenced sprint space, no off-leash freedom, and no small pets.
vibe_summary: An amber-eyed sprinter that literally blushes when happy.

name: Pit Bull Mix
description: The most common dog in American shelters is also one of the most misjudged: a well-raised pit-type mix is a grinning, wiggling, human-obsessed athlete that tests among the most people-affectionate dogs anywhere. They can be choosy about other dogs, so thoughtful introductions matter — but for pure devotion per pound, almost nothing competes.
vibe_summary: A misunderstood love sponge with a blockhead grin.

name: Plott Hound
description: North Carolina's state dog descends from German boar hounds and remains a serious, gritty big-game tracker with a distinctive brindle coat and a voice that carries for miles. Working-bred and tenacious, it is a loyal family dog for active rural homes and a frustrated foghorn in an apartment.
vibe_summary: A brindle mountain hunter with grit to spare and a bark that carries counties.

name: Pointer
description: The English Pointer is bird-finding distilled: a lean, hard-driving athlete that freezes into its namesake statue at the faintest whiff of quail. Sweet and even-tempered in the house once exercised, but the exercise clause is non-negotiable and measured in miles, not walks.
vibe_summary: A living compass needle that runs all day and dozes all evening.

name: Pomeranian
description: A sled dog shrunk to six pounds, the Pomeranian kept the spitz confidence, the double coat, and the conviction that it is in charge of perimeter security. Smart and lively, it excels in trick training but will bark at everything unless taught otherwise early.
vibe_summary: A pocket lion with a sled dog's ego and a foghorn's dedication.

name: Portuguese Water Dog
description: Once crew on Portuguese fishing boats, herding fish into nets and carrying messages between vessels, the PWD is a webbed-footed workaholic that made the White House look easy. It offers retriever energy in a low-shedding package, provided you supply water, work, and regular clipping.
vibe_summary: A curly-coated deckhand still looking for a boat to work.

name: Pug
description: The motto multum in parvo, a lot in a little, fits a dog that packs outsized comedy, appetite, and devotion into a wrinkled sixteen-pound frame. Pugs shed far more than their short coat suggests, gain weight on air, and their flat faces make heat and airline cargo holds genuinely dangerous.
vibe_summary: A wheezing stand-up comedian who lives for snacks and your undivided attention.

name: Puggle
description: A Pug-Beagle cross that pairs the Pug's clownish devotion with the Beagle's nose-driven curiosity, wrapped in a sturdier, longer-muzzled body. Expect a cheerful shadow who follows scents down the sidewalk and follows you onto the couch, with occasional Beagle-grade howling.
vibe_summary: A snuffling comedian who thinks every walk is a treasure hunt.

name: Rat Terrier
description: An American farm dog bred to clear barns of vermin, and it still moves like it has a job to do — quick, athletic, and absurdly durable for its size. Smarter and more biddable than most terriers, it bonds hard to its people while keeping one eye on the squirrels.
vibe_summary: A pocket-sized athlete with a farmhand's work ethic.

name: Redbone Coonhound
description: A flame-coated Southern treeing hound with a bawling voice that carries for miles and a temperament far mellower than its hunting résumé suggests. At home it is affectionate and easygoing, but the nose overrules the ears the moment a trail crosses its path.
vibe_summary: A sweet-natured crooner who lives by his nose.

name: Rhodesian Ridgeback
description: Bred in southern Africa to track lions and hold them at bay, the Ridgeback is a powerful, quiet athlete with the signature ridge of reversed hair along its spine. Dignified and aloof with strangers, it needs an owner who leads calmly — this is not a dog that begs for direction.
vibe_summary: A lion-country aristocrat who guards without theatrics.

name: Rottweiler
description: A Roman drover's dog turned modern guardian, the Rottweiler is confident, calm, and startlingly trainable when its considerable mind is engaged. With its own family it is a leaning, goofy shadow; with strangers it is all watchful reserve, which demands early and lifelong socialization.
vibe_summary: A velvet-hearted bodyguard who takes the job seriously.

name: Saint Bernard
description: The Alpine rescue legend is exactly the gentle mountain of a dog it appears to be — patient with children, unhurried in everything, and happiest sprawled across the coolest floor in the house. Budget for drool towels, serious food bills, and a heartbreakingly short lifespan.
vibe_summary: A slow-motion avalanche of slobbery devotion.

name: Saluki
description: One of the oldest dog breeds on earth, the Saluki is a desert sighthound of feathery elegance and near-feline reserve, capable of running down gazelle and equally capable of ignoring your recall. It gives affection on its own schedule and expects the same courtesy of quiet dignity in return.
vibe_summary: Ancient desert royalty that tolerates your admiration.

name: Samoyed
description: The famous "Sammy smile" is functional — it keeps the drool from freezing — and it perfectly matches this Siberian sled dog's relentlessly sunny, people-obsessed temperament. The dazzling white coat sheds in drifts and demands real grooming commitment, and a bored Samoyed will narrate its complaints loudly.
vibe_summary: A smiling cloud that talks back and hates being left out.

name: Schipperke
description: The little black Belgian barge dog is a fearless, fox-faced busybody that patrolled canal boats for rats and intruders and still treats your home as its ship. Mischievous and opinionated, it packs big-dog watchfulness into a cat-sized frame that lives well into its teens.
vibe_summary: A tiny black captain who runs a very tight ship.

name: Schnoodle
description: The Schnauzer-Poodle cross stacks two of the smartest low-shedding breeds into one alert, curly, endlessly teachable companion. It inherits the Schnauzer's watchful streak and the Poodle's love of performance, so expect a dog that learns tricks fast and announces the mail faster.
vibe_summary: A curly quick-study who moonlights as your doorbell.

name: Scottish Terrier
description: The bearded, dignified Scottie is a terrier of strong opinions — independent, stubborn, and deeply loyal to a chosen few rather than the whole neighborhood. It carries itself like a much larger dog and expects to be negotiated with, not commanded.
vibe_summary: A whiskered Scottish gentleman who doesn't suffer fools.

name: Shar Pei
description: Behind the famous wrinkles and hippo muzzle is a serious, self-possessed Chinese guardian that bonds tightly to its family and regards everyone else with cool suspicion. The folds and unique coat come with real skin, eye, and fever-syndrome health baggage that owners must plan for.
vibe_summary: A wrinkled stoic who loves few and trusts fewer.

name: Shepherd Mix
description: The classic pointy-eared shelter silhouette usually means German Shepherd or herding heritage blended with something sturdier, producing a smart, watchful dog that bonds hard and learns fast. Mixed genetics typically sidestep the purebred GSD's hip and back troubles, giving you the loyalty without as much of the vet bill.
vibe_summary: Shepherd brains and devotion with a healthier deck of genes.

name: Shetland Sheepdog
description: A miniature herding genius from the Shetland Islands, the Sheltie combines near-Border-Collie brains with a devoted, sensitive nature that makes it one of the most trainable small dogs alive. The trade-offs are a heavy double coat and a hair-trigger bark that announces everything from delivery trucks to falling leaves.
vibe_summary: A brilliant, feathery perfectionist with a lot to say.

name: Shiba Inu
description: Japan's fox-faced national treasure is bold, fastidious, and famously cat-like — it grooms itself, keeps its own counsel, and considers obedience a suggestion. The infamous "Shiba scream" and an escape-artist streak are real, but so is the quiet, self-cleaning companionship for owners who respect its terms.
vibe_summary: A meme-famous fox who loves you but won't admit it.

name: Shih Tzu
description: Bred purely to warm the laps of Chinese emperors, the Shih Tzu has spent a thousand years perfecting the art of being adored, and it shows in its sweet, outgoing, everyone-is-a-friend temperament. The flowing coat needs daily attention or a low-key puppy cut, and the flat face means summer heat is a genuine hazard.
vibe_summary: A tiny imperial lapdog who assumes you exist to dote on it.

name: Siberian Husky
description: Built by the Chukchi people to haul sleds across frozen distances, the Husky is a friendly, dramatic, endlessly athletic escape artist that howls instead of barks and treats fences as puzzles. It loves everyone — which makes it a terrible guard dog — and it will destroy a bored household with cheerful efficiency.
vibe_summary: A wolf-styled drama major with marathon legs and zero guard instinct.

name: Silky Terrier
description: Australia's answer to the Yorkie is a shade bigger, a shade scrappier, and every bit as glamorous, with a flowing steel-and-tan coat over a genuine ratting terrier's engine. It wants more action than its lapdog looks suggest and will happily police the household from the back of the sofa.
vibe_summary: A glamour coat hiding a real terrier's attitude.

name: Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier
description: Ireland's farm terrier greets the world with the famous "Wheaten greetin'" — an exuberant, airborne hello that never fully mellows with age. The silky, low-shed coat mats fast without regular work, and beneath the teddy-bear look sits a genuine terrier who chases first and asks later.
vibe_summary: A bouncing wheat-colored optimist who greets you at altitude.

name: Staffordshire Bull Terrier
description: Known in its native England as the "nanny dog," the Stafford is a compact slab of muscle whose defining trait is an almost embarrassing adoration of humans, children especially. It can be selective with other dogs, so early socialization matters, but with people it is pure, grinning devotion.
vibe_summary: A muscle-bound softie who thinks every human is family.

name: Standard Poodle
description: Strip away the show clips and the Standard Poodle is a rugged German duck retriever that consistently ranks among the two or three smartest breeds on earth. It is an elegant, low-allergen family athlete whose only real demands are daily exercise, mental work, and a standing grooming budget.
vibe_summary: A duck-hunting intellectual unfairly typecast by its haircut.

name: Standard Schnauzer
description: The original mid-size Schnauzer is a bearded German farm all-rounder — ratter, watchdog, and family sentinel — with sharp wits and a robust, long-lived body. It is clever enough to outmaneuver a passive owner and thrives when given real jobs and firm, fair rules.
vibe_summary: A bearded strategist who audits everyone entering the house.

name: Swedish Vallhund
description: The "Viking dog" is a long-bodied, corgi-adjacent cattle herder that sailed with Norse raiders a thousand years ago and still carries itself with cheerful, big-dog confidence. Energetic, vocal, and endlessly engaged, it makes a hardy little companion for active households.
vibe_summary: A Viking longship's dog compressed into corgi form.

name: Terrier Mix
description: The scruffy little "what exactly is that?" dog is a shelter mainstay: wiry-coated, big-personality mixes that pack terrier boldness and comedy into an apartment-friendly frame with famously long lifespans. Whatever the ingredients, you reliably get spark, loyalty, and a standing feud with the local squirrels.
vibe_summary: A scruffy wildcard with a big personality and a bigger opinion of itself.

name: Tibetan Mastiff
description: An ancient Himalayan flock guardian that worked alone at altitude, the Tibetan Mastiff is majestic, territorial, and profoundly independent — it was bred to make its own decisions, and it still does. Nocturnal barking and deep suspicion of strangers make it a serious commitment, not a trophy.
vibe_summary: A lion-maned mountain sovereign who answers to no one.

name: Tibetan Terrier
description: Not a terrier at all, this shaggy monastery companion was raised by Tibetan lamas as a bringer of luck, and its snowshoe-flat feet still grip like it lives on a mountainside. Sensitive, adaptable, and long-lived, it is affectionate with its family and politely watchful with everyone else.
vibe_summary: A shaggy monastery good-luck charm with mountaineer's feet.

name: Toy Poodle
description: The smallest Poodle carries the same first-class brain as its bigger siblings, which makes it one of the few toy breeds that genuinely enjoys training sessions. It is a long-lived, devoted apartment companion, though its tiny frame is too delicate for boisterous small children.
vibe_summary: A six-pound scholar who'd rather learn a trick than sit still.

name: Treeing Walker Coonhound
description: The "people's choice" of American coonhounds is fast, loud, and single-minded on a trail, with a chopping bark it deploys generously and a sweet, sociable off-duty personality. Southern shelters overflow with them, making this athletic, tolerant hound one of rescue's best-kept secrets.
vibe_summary: A big-voiced Southern athlete who's all sweetness off the trail.

name: Vizsla
description: Hungary's russet-gold pointer is the definitive velcro dog — a sensitive, gifted athlete that needs to run hard daily and then physically drape itself over its person to recover. Leave it alone or under-exercised and it unravels; meet its needs and you get one of the most devoted sporting dogs ever bred.
vibe_summary: A golden shadow that runs ten miles, then sits on your lap.

name: Weimaraner
description: The "Gray Ghost" was bred for German nobility to hunt big game, and it retains a noble's sense of entitlement to your time, your bed, and your undivided attention. Brilliant and physically relentless, it punishes boredom and solitude with legendary destructive creativity.
vibe_summary: A silver aristocrat with separation anxiety and an engine that won't quit.

name: Welsh Springer Spaniel
description: The red-and-white cousin of the English Springer is a steadier, more reserved bird dog that saves its considerable affection for its own family. It is a tireless field companion with an off switch at home, though it wilts emotionally if left out of family life.
vibe_summary: A devoted red-and-white countryman, shy with strangers, all heart at home.

name: Welsh Terrier
description: A scaled-down Airedale in spirit and coat, the Welsh Terrier is spirited, sturdy, and a touch calmer than the average terrier — though "calm" here is graded on the terrier curve. Its wiry black-and-tan jacket barely sheds, and its confidence never wavers.
vibe_summary: The Airedale's mini-me: cheerful, wiry, and always game.

name: West Highland White Terrier
description: The Westie carries classic Scottish terrier grit inside an irresistibly cheerful white package, making it one of the friendliest and most adaptable of the earthdogs. It still digs, chases, and argues like a terrier, but it does so with a grin that gets it out of trouble.
vibe_summary: Sunshine in a white wire coat, with a terrier's fine print.

name: Whippet
description: The fastest accelerating dog on earth spends roughly 23 hours a day as a warm, silent, blanket-burrowing noodle, and one hour as a 35-mph missile. Gentle, quiet, and nearly odorless, the Whippet is arguably the easiest sighthound — and one of the easiest dogs, period — to actually live with.
vibe_summary: A rocket that idles as a heated couch ornament.

name: Wirehaired Pointing Griffon
description: Nicknamed the "supreme gundog," the Griffon is a bearded, weatherproof hunting partner that points, retrieves, and swims with equal enthusiasm, then settles into affable family life. Its harsh coat sheds little, and its temperament is among the most even-keeled in the sporting world.
vibe_summary: A scruffy-bearded outdoorsman who's great with everybody.

name: Xoloitzcuintli
description: The 3,000-year-old Mexican hairless dog was sacred to the Aztecs as a guide for souls, and it remains a calm, watchful, radiator-warm companion with primitive-breed sharpness toward strangers. No coat means sunscreen and sweaters, but also no shedding and remarkable overall health.
vibe_summary: An ancient Aztec hot-water bottle with a guard's instincts.

name: Yorkipoo
description: This Yorkie-Poodle cross blends terrier sass with Poodle smarts in a barely-shedding package small enough for any apartment. It is livelier and mouthier than its teddy-bear looks advertise, and it wants to be involved in absolutely everything you do.
vibe_summary: A palm-sized extrovert with Poodle brains and Yorkie opinions.

name: Yorkshire Terrier
description: Bred to kill rats in Victorian textile mills before graduating to Victorian laps, the Yorkie still runs on pure terrier self-belief inside a silky show coat. It is bold to the point of comedy with big dogs, devoted to its person, and far more watchdog than lapdog when the doorbell rings.
vibe_summary: Six pounds of silk-wrapped mill-rat swagger.
